newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Strong demand in Cimpor privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Strong demand in Cimpor privatisation.

text.p: Applications for shares have comfortably outstripped supply a week before pre-registration ends in the second stage of the privatisation of Portuguese cement group Cimpor, a source familiar with the process said on Monday.
"Applications for shares have already comfortably exceeded the number of shares available," the source, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.

The source said that in the first week of pre-registration applications had been lodged for more than 63 million shares, well above the 37.8 million available in the privatisation of a 45 percent stake of Portugal's biggest cement producer.
Small investors had submitted some three quarters of the applications so far, the source added.
"The strong demand is due to the financial solidity of the company and expectations of good dividends," the source said.
Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal said this month that full 1996 net profit would be at least double the 11.6 billion escudos ($75 million) posted in the first six months of the year.
The company made a consolidated net profit of 18.4 billion escudos ($118 million) in 1995.
The source said the demand for Cimpor shares was stronger than for Portugal Telecom at the same stage of its pre-registration.
The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres sold off a second 22 percent tranche of Portugal Telecom in a comfortably oversubscribed sale in June.
Cimpor, which could be worth more than 120 billion escudos ($776 million), will benefit from a healthy construction sector in the run-up to Lisbon's 1998 World Fair, analysts said.
Company officials have said Cimpor could use its cash mountain to buy foreign cement producers after the selloff.

Pre-registration in the Cimpor privatisation continues until October 4. An international roadshow to promote the sale proceeds until October 11. Lisbon bourse will announce the results of the privatisation on October 15.
The previous Social Democrat government sold off a 20 percent stake in Cimpor.

Prime Minister Guterres said in New York earlier this month that the state could raise 450 billion escudos ($2.9 billion) from privatisations in 1996, well above its target of 380 billion ($2.4 billion).
Cimpor shares stood at 3,264 escudos, up eight, in volume of 9,299 shares in early afternoon trade.
